Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Details how to diagnose flawed ROAS metrics in Meta ad accounts by utilizing audience breakdowns and attribution windows, demonstrating that top-spending ads often over-index on retargeting returning customers and view-through conversions rather than driving incremental new customer acquisition. modules: [ADC] topics: [attribution and modeling, campaign setup and tracking] tier: 2 scope_hint: core

Topics. attribution and modeling / Deconstructing deceptive Return on Ad Spend (ROAS) metrics within Meta Advantage+ campaigns by demonstrating how a seemingly strong 13x ROAS often masks poor performance (e.g., a 1.7x incremental ROAS) once analyzed through the lens of audience breakdowns (existing vs. new customers) and attribution settings (7-day click vs. 1-day view). Differentiating between a true Conversion Lift Test (a geo-holdout experiment based on difference-in-difference design) and Meta's "incremental attribution" setting (an algorithmic estimate based on aggregated competitor data), advising against using the latter for campaign optimization. campaign setup and tracking / Establishing strict account structure guidelines to prevent top-of-funnel scaling campaigns from cannibalizing retargeting audiences. Mandating the use of a 7-day click attribution setting for optimization (ignoring view-throughs) and explicitly excluding existing customers from cold campaigns (with specific nuances for lapsed customers, e.g., excluding 2-year purchasers). Recommending that scaling efforts be measured against top-line revenue impact—specifically, new customer sales at the individual SKU level—rather than relying solely on in-platform ROAS.

Look for. The primary reason a top-spending ad in an Advantage+ campaign might actually be performing poorly: it is over-allocating budget to existing customers and relying heavily on 1-day view-through conversions rather than driving incremental new customers. The recommended attribution setting for campaign optimization: 7-day click. The distinction between a Meta Conversion Lift Test and Meta's "incremental attribution" setting: a lift test is a true holdout experiment, whereas the incremental setting is merely an algorithmic estimate based on competitor averages. The primary method to verify ad scaling success: measuring top-line new customer sales at the specific SKU level in Shopify.
Skip. General complaints about other agencies misinterpreting data.
